description: Polyphonic chord sequencer: it records the gates and pitches of a held chord into one of 16 steps and plays those chords back in one of eight orders

params.text: Chooses which step is recorded into or played, 1 to 16; with the clock stopped, turning it auditions each step, and it follows the sequencer while the clock runs
Switches between recording and playing; while recording, every note held during a gate is written into the current step and the step advances when the gate falls
Sets how many steps the sequence runs for, 1 to 16, counting steps whether or not anything has been recorded into them
Returns the sequencer to the first step of the sequence, which is not step 1 in every mode
Steps through the four plain modes of forward, backward, random without repeats, and step chosen by CV; holding it for a second switches to the four hidden modes of skip, ping-pong, shuffle and glide
Turns on offset mode, in which the STEP knob sets the first step of the sequence instead of the current one and stops following the sequencer

inputs.text: Chooses the step in the CV and glide modes, 0-5V across the sequence length; in skip mode it sets the chance of skipping a step over 0-10V, and 20% when nothing is patched
A trigger or a gate here returns the sequencer to the first step of the sequence
Advances the sequencer one step, or retriggers the current step in the modes that pick steps by CV; it is read only in play state
Polyphonic gates saying which notes to record; the channel count has to match the module's poly channel setting or some notes go unrecorded
Polyphonic pitches, recorded into the current step for as long as the gate input is high
Sets the sequence length while a cable is patched, 0-5V giving 1 to 16 steps, in place of the LENGTH knob

outputs.text: Polyphonic gates for the step being played, high for as long as the clock input is high
Polyphonic pitches for the step being played, ordered low to high; where a chord uses fewer channels than the module has, the spare channels hold the notes of the chord before it

notes: the steps of a new module are empty and it plays nothing: switch it to record, hold a chord at the gate and pitch inputs to write it into the current step, and switch back to play
playback needs a clock patched to the clock input; a step is taken on a rising edge there and the gate output is high for as long as that clock is high
thirteen factory chord sets are shipped as presets, reached from Rack's own preset menu, among them C Maj Triads, C Maj Jazz Standard and Eb Maj Moody Jazz
when the module is bypassed both outputs stay at 0V
the module follows the VCV timing standard, which locks the clock out for 1ms after a reset
menu: Play Mode — switches between Record and Play, the same two states as the button on the panel
Step Knob Offset Mode — Off leaves the STEP knob choosing the current step, On makes it set the step the sequence starts from
SEQ Mode — picks the sequencing mode by name, from Forward, Backward, Random, CV Control, Skip, Ping Pong, Shuffle and Glide
Polyphony channels — sets how many notes a step can store, five by default
Dynamic Poly Channels — Yes makes the gate output carry as many channels as the step has notes, which can click on some voices; No holds the channel count fixed
Skip Partial Clock — Yes holds any change of step or gate until the next whole clock, which is what to turn on when the module will not stay in step with another sequencer
Step CV Range — sets what the STEP CV input reads, from 0 to 5V, White Keys where C is step 1 and D is step 2, and 0 to 10V
CV Record Order — sets how the channels of one chord are stored: Sorted low to high, Condensed with silent channels dropped, or Pristine as they arrived
Transpose SEQ — shifts every note of every step by a chosen number of semitones, from -12 to +12 with the interval named beside each; the original pitches are not kept
